description: What the developer pays Neblla: the Pro subscription of a PROJECT (€10 a month per project, or $10 outside Europe, taxes included; every app of a Pro project shares its own pool of 2000 credits a day and stops drawing from the account's free pool) and one-off quota packs (they go to the pool the project draws from now: the account's for a free project, the project's own while it is Pro). Name the project with projectId, or name an app (appId) and it is that app's project (neblla_projects "list" says which apps are where; most accounts only have Explorer). "pro_checkout" and "quota_pack_checkout" return a URL the DEVELOPER opens to pay — an agent cannot complete a payment, and nothing is granted until Stripe confirms it, so tell them the upgrade lands a few seconds after they finish. "cancel_pro" stops Pro from renewing: it stays until the end of the period already paid (answers endsAt) and then the project is Free; nothing is refunded. Only call it when the developer has asked for it in as many words. "resume_pro" takes a pending cancellation back while that period lasts: Pro renews again on the same date (answers renewsAt), nothing is paid now; once Pro has ended, it is a new pro_checkout. While a cancellation is pending, pro_checkout answers pro_ending (with endsAt) instead of a link: offer resume_pro. "auto_recharge" { appId, enabled, monthlyCap (euros) }: OPTIONAL — when the pool of that app runs out of quota, buy one more pack with the card of their last pack, up to the monthly cap (required); an email on each recharge and at the cap. Without enabled/monthlyCap it answers the current state. Only when the developer asks for it. Selling to users is a different thing — that is neblla_payments_account plus neblla_create_product.

appId.description: An app: its project (required for auto_recharge)

monthlyCap.description: auto_recharge: the most it may spend in a month, in euros (required to switch it on)

name: neblla_billing
